item.title: Iran weighs resuming oil exports in defiance of US naval blockade – IRGC outlet
item.summary: A satellite image shows an oil terminal at Kharg Island, Iran ...
item.page_text:
Iran is considering resuming oil exports despite the US naval blockade, the Revolutionary Guards-affiliated Sabereen News reported, hours after the oil tracker TankerTrackers said Iran “appears to be preparing to ship out oil again.”
In an earlier post marked “unofficial,” Sabereen said dozens of Iranian tankers were preparing to sail for China. It also claimed Tehran had warned countries across the region that it would go to war if the United States attacked the tankers on their way to China.
His five-year term, which began in September 2021, ended on September 29 amid criticism over declining audiences, political imbalance and the perceived domination of the broadcaster by figures associated with the ultrahardline Paydari Front.
The eventual appointment, which must be made by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, could signal whether the leadership intends to curb the influence of hardline factions associated with Saeed Jalili or preserve their dominance over the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), which holds a constitutional monopoly over domestic radio and television broadcasting.
Jalili, who has promoted the idea of a “shadow government,” is a key member of the Supreme National Security Council. His brother, Vahid Jalili, serves as the broadcaster's deputy chief and oversees much of its content.
Several other figures associated with the hardline faction were appointed to senior positions across the broadcaster's channels after 2021.
IRIB is a central instrument for agenda-setting, elite messaging and crisis management, and one of the principal platforms through which the Supreme Leader's office communicates with the public.
Its leadership also controls a vast patronage network encompassing thousands of managerial, editorial and production appointments.
Unlike ministers or executives of state-owned companies, the head of IRIB is not selected by parliament, the government or the broadcaster's supervisory council.
Under Article 175 of the Iranian Constitution, the head of IRIB is appointed directly by the Supreme Leader.
The six-member supervisory council, whose members are drawn from the executive, legislative and judicial branches, oversees the organization but does not choose its chief executive and generally exercises little influence over day-to-day management.
In practice, informal consultations take place among key political, security and cultural actors. The Supreme Leader's office assesses potential candidates, while factional lobbying emerges through media leaks and elite networks.
Ultimately, the Supreme Leader issues a decree either appointing a new chief or extending the incumbent's term.
The political realignment following the crises of 2025–26 has made the succession unusually consequential.
In mid-October, Jomhouri Eslami , citing unofficial sources, reported that the decision to replace Jebelli had already been made and that several names were under consideration. Yet no announcement has followed.
One possible explanation is factional deadlock. Reappointing Jebelli would likely upset parts of the establishment that have criticized his tenure, while removing him could provoke resistance from Jalili's supporters.
Another factor may be uncertainty over decision-making authority under Mojtaba Khamenei. More than eight months after becoming Supreme Leader, he has made no public appearance, and no authenticated audio or video recording of him has been released. Whether this has contributed to the delay remains unclear.
Delays in senior appointments also occurred under Ali Khamenei. Yet the contrast with other recent decisions is notable. Mojtaba Khamenei reappointed Judiciary Chief Gholamhossein Mohseni-Ejei in June, just three days after the expiration of his previous term.
A similar institutional limbo has surrounded the Intelligence Ministry for more than eight months since the death of former Intelligence Minister Esmaeil Khatib.
The prolonged silence over IRIB may therefore reveal something about the new Supreme Leader's authority and decision-making style, particularly his ability or willingness to resolve competing demands within the political establishment.
Under Jebelli, the broadcaster became a stronghold of the anti-negotiation camp. For years, hardline factions skeptical of engagement with the United States have used IRIB as a platform to undermine pragmatic efforts to improve relations with Washington.
The next appointment could therefore serve as an early indicator of the postwar balance between advocates of confrontation and supporters of diplomacy, as well as the new leadership's broader orientation toward negotiations with the United States.
Other factors heighten the importance of the decision, including significant audience erosion and IRIB's strained relationship with President Massoud Pezeshkian's administration.
Several senior officials, including Pezeshkian, have publicly criticized aspects of its coverage, while critics argue that IRIB has increasingly functioned as a platform for specific ideological factions rather than a genuinely national broadcaster.
Although Iranian media outlets have identified several potential successors, most speculation remains tentative. Few observers have a clear understanding of Mojtaba Khamenei's views, making predictions particularly difficult.
Broadly speaking, three scenarios could shape the broadcaster's future.
The first is that Jebelli remains in office, suggesting that the leadership is broadly satisfied with the current direction despite mounting criticism.
The second involves appointing a successor from the Jalili network. Selecting someone already serving within IRIB's senior leadership would signal continuity with the ideological transformation that began after 2021.

item.title: Satellite images show a collapsed span of the Crimean Bridge after Ukraine's third strike in a week
item.summary: Satellite images show a collapsed span of the Crimean Bridge after Ukraine's third strike in a week. November 19, 2026, 10:11 am. Source: Meduza.
item.page_text:
Ukrainian OSINT channels published satellite images of the Crimean Bridge taken on November 19, after three Ukrainian attacks in a single week.
The images show damage to the bridge’s roadway and the parallel rail line. One roadway span collapsed into the water.
Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge on three nights in the past week: November 15-16, November 16-17, and November 18-19. The third strike came just before a meeting in China between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping. After the second attack, a video recorded from a train crossing the bridge was posted on social media. The video shows that one of the bridge’s roadway spans had collapsed completely. Rail traffic on the bridge was temporarily suspended after the strikes but resumed on November 19.
At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication.
If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at [email protected] .

item.title: Sentinel-3C satellite images show heat contrast between Morocco and Spain - Bladi.net
item.summary: Sentinel-3C satellite images show heat contrast between Morocco and Spain. The European Space Agency (ESA) has just unveiled the first thermal ...
item.page_text:
The images published on Wednesday, November 18 were captured on November 2. They show Morocco, Algeria, the Iberian Peninsula and part of France. According to the ESA, temperatures in some areas of Morocco exceed 30 °C on the thermal map, compared with around 25 to 30 °C in Andalusia and southern Portugal.
On Bladi.net : Morocco’s mysterious red patch visible from space reveals thriving desert agriculture
These measurements are known as “brightness temperatures” and are calculated from infrared radiation captured at the top of the atmosphere. They differ from air temperatures recorded by weather stations.
A second image, produced in false color, reveals contrasts between the landscapes. Areas of dense vegetation appear bright green and generally correspond to the coolest surfaces on the thermal map. The sensors also make it possible to observe temperature differences between land and the waters of the Atlantic and Mediterranean.
On Bladi.net : Morocco: Satellite images reveal a country transformed by record rainfall
Launched on September 15, 2026, Sentinel-3C carries a radiometer capable of observing land and sea surfaces in nine spectral bands. Two additional channels are dedicated to detecting and tracking fires. These first thermal images confirm that the instrument is working properly, while it is still in the commissioning phase.

The attack hit the Kalyekino pumping station, threatening crude supplies to refineries and export terminals thousands of miles away.

why: Satellite pic of bridge destruction with before-image; tabloid framing, same scene as others.

draft.skip_reason: Reuse policy is link_only with no image credit or licence on the page, and the only source is a partisan tabloid war report that gives no date, sensor or resolution for the satellite image.
draft.what_it_shows: According to The Sun, satellite imagery captured by US firm Vantor shows the Crimean Bridge after three Ukrainian strikes in a week, with a 740ft (about 225 m) gap where the road arch collapsed. Vantor reportedly said it had seen no repair efforts on or near the damaged bridge. The page gives no capture date, sensor, resolution or image credit line.
uncertainties: Reuse policy is link_only and no image licence is stated, so the image cannot be reposted as a square.
No verbatim image credit on the page. Vantor is named as the firm that captured the images, but not as a credit line.
No capture date, sensor or resolution given for the satellite image.

The text is internally inconsistent: it calls the 740ft collapse both the result of the 'latest' onslaught and of a strike 'two days ago'. It says the latest attack hit the rail crossing but also that the rail arch 'reportedly remained intact'.
Claims about strike methods (drone swarms, ballistic and cruise missiles) and planning by Ukrainian intelligence are unsourced tabloid assertions.
Heavily partisan framing ('tyrant', 'puppet governor') and an active conflict topic, which does not suit Geoawesome's tone.
If the editor wants to cover this, look for Vantor's own release, which would carry a licence, a credit and a capture date.
